# `discarded-error`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports an empty `catch {}` body.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Silently converting failure into success hides the original error and lets
execution continue with an unverified result.

## When it fires

It fires on an empty `catch {}` body. A comment inside the body, on the same
line or on a comment line just above the statement counts as the
justification, and so does an explicit `_ = f() catch {};` discard. A catch
whose error has no caller left to tell is exempt: one in a `defer` or
`errdefer` cleanup, in the body of an enclosing `catch` or `else |err|`, or in
a block that ends by returning an error. So are best-effort calls: terminal
styling (`setColor`, `setAttribute`), `flush`, thread naming (`setName`),
cleanup that closes, deletes, removes, unlinks, kills, cancels or destroys, a
write to stderr, and the std helpers `unexpectedErrno`, `unexpectedStatus`
and `errnoBug`, which log a status and return it as an error. Main-path work
whose failure changes the result stays reported. Enable it when errors must be
handled, propagated, or explicitly justified rather than ignored.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn run() !void {}

pub fn main() void {
    run() catch {};
}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Errors>
